To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

depletion of the major heat-shock protein Hsp72 in tumor cells causes activation of a senescence program, leading to a defect in the activation of the Chk1 kinase in response to genotoxic stress and to increased sensitivity to DNA damaging agents.

depletion of the major heat-shock protein Hsp72 in tumor cells leads to activation of senescence programs and sensitizes cells for genotoxic stresses, and the underlying mechanism involves suppression of Chk-1 activation.
Hsp72-depletion leads to suppression of Chk kinase and sensitizes the cells to genotoxic stress.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular mechanisms that underlie cellular aging and the role of the heat shock protein HSP70 in the process of cellular senescence.
the role of the heat shock protein HSP72 in cell cycle checkpoint and DNA repair.
the role of Hsp72 in the DNA damage checkpoint response and the consequences of the Hsp72 chaperone imbalance on cell survival.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the senescence response is a stress response and that it is activated in response to a number of stress stimuli.
HSP72 depletion leads to a defect in Chk activation which in turn leads to an increase in sensitivity of the cell to genotoxic stimuli.
the Hsp70 chaperone system is a critical component of DNA damage response and that its deficiency results in a defect in the inter-S checkpoint and in increased sensitivity to DNA damaging agents.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
depletion of Hsp72 triggers the senescence pathway, which in turn leads to inhibition of Chk1 kinase, defective checkpoint response, and increased sensitivity of cells to DNA-damaging agents.
the Hsp70 chaperone system plays an important role in the DNA damage checkpoint response, and that its depletion may lead to increased sensitivity of cells to DNA damaging agents.
the senescence pathway suppresses Chk-1 kinase activity and sensitizes cells for genotoxic stresses.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the senescence pathway is not only involved in cell cycle arrest, but also in the regulation of DNA repair.
senescence is not only a tumor-suppressive mechanism, but also a mechanism that can be exploited by tumors to gain resistance to genotoxic stresses.
the DNA damage response is not an all-or-nothing phenomenon and can be modulated in a selective manner.
